[32011 Multilayer Switched Networks | Subject description]
Credit points: 6

This subject advances your understanding and practical skills in designing and implementing switched campus networks, using VLANs to enhance performance, reliability, management, and security. You'll explore various approaches to plan, configure, and verify complex enterprise switching solutions, with hands-on experience on Cisco Systems layer 2 and layer 3 switches. The curriculum aligns with CCNP Enterprise: Core Networking (ENCOR) and is conducted at the UTS Cisco Systems Network Academy.

[32011 Multilayer Switched Networks | Learning and teaching activities]
4 contact hours per week, consisting of lecture and a combined tutorial and laboratory session.

Most factual contents are available as online course materials with e-laboratories, pre-tests and other learning support activities. Students are required to study the online materials and complete any assigned activities before class so that informed debate on issues is possible. Instructors will conduct classes on the understanding that all students have completed the required pre-study, and will make use of this pre-study during the class time.

Lab activities plays significant role to enhance students’ understanding on knowledge learnt in lecture and improve students’ hands-on skills. Students are strongly encouraged to complete the lab activities in networking labs in UTS campus. If lab access is not available in certain cases, students are suggested to complete the necessary lab activities using software recommended.

The subject is run in the UTS Cisco Systems Network Academy. The subject is part of a sequence which will allow students to prepare for CCNP industry certification.

Expected commitment time: 7 hours/week. Additional time will be required on the assignments.

title: Learning outcomes
content:
[32011 Multilayer Switched Networks | Learning outcomes]
SLO1: Evaluate the design benefits and limitations of switched campus networks by applying knowledge of the theoretical characteristics of different high-speed switched network technologies. (C.1)
SLO2: Apply appropriate switched network technologies to meet needs of switched networks. (C.1)
SLO3: Apply troubleshooting steps to solve problems encountered in switched LANs. (D.1)
SLO4: Explain to technically informed people the merits of different modes of network configurations. (D.1)

[32011 Multilayer Switched Networks | Requisites]
Before you enrol in this subject, you must ensure you have met its requisites. The requisites for this subject can be viewed on its access conditions page.

[32011 Multilayer Switched Networks | Additional subject details]
Additional costs
UTS offers a fully-equipped lab environment for completing course-related activities. To ensure seamless practice outside class hours and preparedness for unexpected technical challenges, students are advised to prepare the following resources before classes begin:

1. USB 3.0 Flash Drive (16GB Minimum)

- Students must have a USB 3.0 portable storage device with a minimum 16 GB capacity.

- This drive will be used to store a pre-configured Virtual Machine (VM), which serves as a backup during lab sessions in case of unexpected technical issues with primary lab software.

- The VM may also be used for at-home practice, provided your personal computer meets the specifications below.

2. Personal Computer Specifications

- RAM: Minimum 16GB (strongly recommended for optimal VM performance).

- Virtualization Software: VMware Workstation Player (Windows/Linux) or VMware Fusion (Intel-based Macs only; not compatible with M1/M2/M3 processors).

- Internet Access: Required for software updates and accessing course materials.

 

Alternative Solutions for Unsupported Devices

If your computer does not meet the above specifications, you may utilize online software alternatives. Detailed guidance is available in the "Other Documents" section under “Modules” on Canvas.
